Harjyot Singh Bhalla Additional Sessions Judge04 Patiala House Courts, New Delhi In The Matter Of: Jagjit Singh Vs. The State [Govt. Of Nct Of Delhi] Ca No. 47/2023 Jagjit Singh S/o Sh. Kaleecharan M/s Jagjit Halwai, Shop No.4, Behind Hanuman Mandir, Seva Nagar, New Delhi110003 R/o H. No. 164, Village Mathana District Aligarh, U.P. ......Appellant Versus The State [ Govt. of Nct of Delhi] Through Department of Prevention of Food Adulteration [Now office of the Commissioner of Food Safety] A20, Lawrence Road, Industrial Area, New Delhi ......Respondent Date of Institution: 28.02.2023 Ca No. 47/2023 Jagjit Singh Vs. The State (Govt. of Nct of Delhi) 1/10 Date of decision : 29.03.2023 Judgment
texts.facts: The FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of "Coconut Laddu" lying in an open tray bearing no label declaration. It is claimed that the sample of Coconut Laddu was taken as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act. 3. As per complaint, one sample of Coconut Laddu was sent to Public Analyst (PA) who vide his report dated 20.11.2010 found that the sample is adulterated because it contains added vegetable oil which is not declared as ingredient. Accordingly, Sanction/Consent under Section 2 (ia) (a), (b) & (m) of PFA Act, as punishable under Section 16 (1) (a) read with Section 7 of the Act was obtained and complaint was filed. 4. Summons were issued against the accused Jagjit Singh vide order dated 23.03.2011. Accused/appellant has not exercised his right Jagjit Singh Vs. The State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi) 2/10 under Section 13(2) of the PFA Act. 5. A Notice for violation of provisions of the Act punishable under Section 16 (1) (a) of PFA Act, read with Section (a), (b) and (m) of Section 2 (ia) of PFA Act was served upon the appellant, to which appellant pleaded not guilty. 6. The prosecution examined 3 witnesses namely, PW1 Food Safety Officer Sh. V.P.S. Chaudhary, PW2 Retired FA Sh. Shivji Mehto, and PW3 P.R. Jha, Additional Secretary to Chief Minister, New Delhi. 7. The statement of the accused/appellant was recorded under Section 313 Cr.PC in which appellant claimed innocence. 8. Record perused. Arguments have been heard. 9. Firstly, in the present case, there was no public witnesses. 10. During arguments, my attention was drawn to the statement recorded under Section 313 of Cr.PC and for the ease of reference, the relevant portion of statement under Section 313 of Cr.PC is being reproduced hereinbelow: Statement of accused Jagjit Singh S/o Sh. Kaleecharan, agad about 38 years, R/o H. No. 164, village Mathana, District Aligarh, UP, under Section 313 Cr. PC Without oath Q1. It is in evidence against you that on 05.11.2010 at about 11:30 AM, FSO Sh. V. P. S. Chaudhary along with FA Sh. Shivji Mehto and under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh. P. R. Jha visited the premises of M/s Jagjit Singh Halwai, Shop No. 4, Behind Hanuman Mandir, Sewa Nagar, Delhi, where you being the FBO cum proprietor of M/s Jagjit Singh Halwai were found present and were conducting the business of the said premises Jagjit Singh Vs. The State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi) 3/10 where having stored various food articles including "Coconut Laddoos" for sale for human consumption. These "Coconut Laddoos" were lying in an open tray bearing no Jagjit Singh vs . The State [Govt. Of Nct Of on 29 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105252888/ 2 label or declaration.
texts.arguments: Further, the entire case of the Jagjit Singh Vs. The State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi) 6/10 prosecution is that on the Form VI, the accused had only disclosed Coconut Powder, Sugar and Food Grade Colour as ingredients of the Laddu. Reliance in this regard is placed upon the decision in Tara Singh Vs. State, AIR 1951 SC 44 and State of Karnataka Vs. Dashrath, 1991 Cr.LJ 2632. 16. In Dashrath (supra), it was observed and I quote: .... Often we find that a long series of facts are put in one question and the accused is asked to explain. The accused if he is not a very highly Jagjit Singh Vs. The State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi) 7/10 intelligent person with a sharp memory may not even remember all the circumstances put to him while giving his explanation. This may very often lead to miscarriage of justice. ....The Court must question the accused in relation to all incriminating circumstances appearing against the accused. The Law Commission in its 41st Report thought that the stage has not yet been reached for the deletion of Jagjit Singh Vs. The State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi) 8/10 this provision and may be in future, with better education and better facilities for legal aid this matter may have to be reconsidered in the charged circumstances. As the law stands today, Sec. 313 of the Code provides not only the accused an opportunity to explain the circumstances appearing against him, but also the Court an opportunity to have a personal dialogue with the accused to elicit such explanation as he may have to offer free from the fear of being trapped to make an embarrasing admission or statement or of being led to make any statement meant to Jagjit Singh vs . The State [Govt. Of Nct Of on 29 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105252888/ 5 fill up the lacuna in the prosecution case..... (emphasis supplied) 17.
